Tom/Team — attaching the inventory workbook (tabbed) and a quick drawio export. High-level notes:

1) Control plane
- API endpoints: control.redwood.internal (multi-AZ), admin port 8443 (TLS mTLS optional)
- Runs in a managed control cluster in customer VPC (private subnets). Control plane instances are stateless; state is kept in a managed KV (Redis) deployed in a persistent subnet (10.10.12.0/24).
- Control plane needs outbound HTTPS to our telemetry collector (collector.redwood.net) and access to KMS (customer-managed key + Redwood agent).

2) Data plane
- Inference workers live in isolated worker subnets (10.10.20.0/22). They perform model execution and require egress to model storage (S3 endpoints) and occasional external model fetch URLs (whitelisted).
- KV cache is on the same VPC but pinned to a different subnet; we recommend strict SG rules allowing only control-plane IPs + worker pool CIDR.

3) NAT/egress
- We expect a single NAT Gateway per AZ for outbound; customers can route via their egress proxies. If Acme requires an egress firewall, we recommend mapping the worker egress through a central proxy (10.10.30.5) and use static IPs for allowlisting.

Sticky/session affinity
- By default the serving runtime uses short-lived affinity keyed by request ID for KV locality; no long-running sticky sessions. Session affinity only required when using pinned GPU reservations — mark in the inventory if you plan to reserve nodes.

Attachments: vpc-splitplane-inventory.xlsx, control-data-flow-v2.drawio

Ben

Thanks Ben — added ops checklist PDF and a short cutover play (see ops-readiness-checklist.pdf). Quick operational clarifications for Acme:

- Pre-cutover smoke tests: small inference job (50 reqs) exercising KV cache warmup and model fetch; validate latency P95 under expected load.
- Rollback trigger: >2% error rate or sustained P95 > 2x baseline for 5 minutes.
- Monitoring hooks: please expose Netflow/flow logs to our ops account for the cutover window (48h) or provide equivalent egress metrics.

Tom — can you confirm if Acme will: (a) provide a dedicated KMS key for session metadata encryption, and (b) if your network team can create the three test IPs for allowlist (we'll send the list)? If yes, we'll schedule the cutover dry-run next week.

Couple of security items to call out before scheduling a dry-run: 

1) KMS integration: we support customer-managed keys (CMKs). For the private deploy we need a cross-account grant for the Redwood agent principal. Tom, if Acme can provision a CMK and grant redwood-agent@redwood-infra role (we'll provide the ARN), we can document the minimal grant surface.

2) Audit/Telemetry: Acme asked for example SOC2 artifacts — Naomi, I'll attach our SOC2 control mapping excerpt in the Confluence doc. If Acme prefers a formal evidence package we can route through Security for a redaction review (SUP-4721).

3) Egress proofing: Ben's suggestion of a central egress proxy is correct for strict allowlist policies. Note that model fetches to public endpoints will need explicit whitelisting; consider mirroring static model layers into a customer S3 to reduce outbound firewall complexity.

I'll update SUP-4721 with the required KMS grant template and link to the SOC2 excerpt.

Karthik
Security, Redwood Inference
